instructions: Pour 2 cups of lukewarm water into a large bowl. It should feel just warm on the inside of your wrist. Sprinkle in the 1 tsp yeast and stir with a fork until it dissolves.
Add the 2 cups flour, the 1 tsp sugar and the 1/2 tsp salt. Whisk until the batter is smooth with no lumps. It should pour slowly off the whisk, a little thicker than ordinary pancake batter.
Cover the bowl with a plate or plastic wrap and leave it somewhere warm for 15 to 20 minutes, until you see bubbles on the surface.
Meanwhile, chop the 1/2 cup walnuts. Warm the 1/2 cup honey in a small pan over low heat for 1 to 2 minutes, until it's runny, then take it off the heat.
Line a plate with paper towels. Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium. It's hot enough when a drop of batter sizzles as soon as it lands.

Drop in heaped tablespoons of batter, 3 or 4 at a time, with room between them. Fry for about 2 minutes, until the underside is golden and the edges look set. Flip them and cook the other side for 1 to 2 minutes, until golden and puffed.
Move them to the lined plate. Add a little more of the oil to the pan before each batch and fry the rest of the batter the same way.
Drizzle the warm honey over the tiganites and scatter the walnuts on top. Serve them warm.
method_notes: All the read versions make a loose batter, fry spoonfuls in a little oil until golden on both sides and serve them warm with honey. My Greek Dish uses a quick yeast batter of flour, water, salt and a pinch of sugar rested 15 to 20 minutes, fried 3 or 4 at a time and topped with warm honey and walnuts. Mia Kouppa rests a thicker yeast batter for an hour and fries in half an inch of oil, and Egg Info skips the yeast for a baking powder batter with eggs, yogurt and honey. This one follows My Greek Dish, so there are no eggs in it.
